channel.title: The Picky Reader — New Releases
channel.description: New and notable theology releases, tracked weekly.

item.title: The Phantom — Bob Drury, Tom Clavin
item.description: Bob Drury and Tom Clavin on Marine Major Pete Ortiz, a former Foreign Legionnaire who ran OSS missions in North Africa and occupied France and earned two Navy Crosses.

item.title: The Great Horse Flu — Thomas G. Andrews
item.description: Thomas Andrews tells of the 1872-73 equine influenza that sickened most of North America's horses and mules, stalled the economy, and fed into the Panic of 1873.

item.title: Charlemagne's Dream — James T. Palmer
item.description: A history of the whole Carolingian dynasty, not Charlemagne alone: the conquests, the alliance with the papacy, the first missions to northern Europe, and the heirs who lost the empire.

item.title: Irreplaceable — Gene Edward Veith Jr. & A. Trevor Sutton
item.description: Gene Veith and Trevor Sutton bring the Reformation doctrine of vocation to the age of AI and automation, asking what work is for when machines can do it. A theology of the human person for the technology question every church is now facing.

item.title: The Whole-Life Pastor — Mark D. Allen
item.description: Pastoral theology shaped by Augustine, and a case that ministry is a way of life before it is a set of tasks. For the pastor who suspects the calling has quietly become a job.

item.title: The Rush — Nathaniel Philbrick
item.description: Philbrick follows the gold as it moves from riverbed to countinghouse to the halls of power, revealing how vigilantism hardened into law and how debates over slavery in the West tipped the balance in Washington.

item.title: The Invention of the Dog — Tamsin Pickeral
item.description: A fascinating illustrated history of humanity's relationship with dogs, tracing how we shaped more than seventy breeds to hunt, guard, herd, retrieve, and above all be loyal companions. From the Pekingese carried by Chinese emperors to the boar-hunting Dachshund, Tamsin Pickeral blends history with anecdote across 160 illustrations. It is a joyful celebration of our centuries-old obsession with man's best friend.

item.title: Justification and the Churches — Gerald Hiestand
item.description: In Justification and the Churches, Gerald Hiestand offers a careful and pastorally framed exploration of how Protestant, Roman Catholic, and Eastern Orthodox traditions articulate the mystery of salvation.

item.title: Finally Home — Dane Ortlund
item.description: In Finally Home, Dane Ortlund ushers readers into the surprising wonders of our final future in the new heavens and the new earth. It provides deep comfort and joy that outweighs all our many…

item.title: The Stories We Live By — Timothy Keller & Michael Keller
item.description: Timothy Keller's last collaboration with his son Michael, reading the culture's governing stories against the one Jesus tells. Broadly evangelical rather than confessional, and vintage Keller in its patience with the person who disagrees.

item.title: Psalms of Trust — H. B. Charles Jr.
item.description: Ten psalms on trusting God when circumstances give no reason to. Charles preaches these as a pastor who has had to, and the brevity is a feature.

item.title: A Librarian's War — Molly Guptill Manning
item.description: Molly Guptill Manning's biography of Ray Trautman, the Army's chief librarian in World War II, who oversaw the distribution of nearly half a billion books and magazines to the troops.

item.title: The City Without Jews — Douglas Smith
item.description: Douglas Smith's history of the destruction of Jewish Vienna under seven years of Nazi rule, built around the letters and diaries of a Jewish nurse who stayed in the city.

item.title: Hope for the Anxious and Depressed — Hope A. Blanton & Christine B. Gordon
item.description: A practical theologian and a clinical social worker on anxiety and depression through the lens of Scripture. Hope Blanton and Christine Gordon write for the sufferer and the friend, not the clinic.

item.title: How Bright the Path Grows — Marcia Chatelain
item.description: Thirteen Black women organized and sang at the 1963 March and were kept off the podium. Chatelain puts them back into the account.

item.title: A Glorious Fate — Kevin M. Levin
item.description: The first Shaw biography in twenty-five years. Levin finds a young man indifferent to his parents' abolitionism, remade by the war into a symbol he never chose.

item.title: The Last Invasion of England — Arthur der Weduwen
item.description: The Glorious Revolution was a seaborne conquest. Der Weduwen counts the sixteen thousand Dutch troops and argues James II fell to an invasion, not a mood.

item.title: Why Christianity Makes Sense — Gavin Ortlund
item.description: For anyone in search of meaningful answers to the mysteries of the world and the purpose for their life, Why Christianity Makes Sense offers a fresh sense of wonder and enchantment at the gospel of Jesus.

item.title: Classical Theology for the Modern Mind — Carl R. Trueman
item.description: In Classical Theology for the Modern Mind, historical scholar Carl Trueman examines how remembering history, reciting creeds, and studying ecclesiology counter cultural pathologies that inhibit…

item.title: The Works of Thomas Watson, 7 Volumes — Thomas Watson · gen. ed. J. Stephen Yuille
item.description: The first definitive collected edition of one of the most-quoted Puritans — now out in a definitive collected edition.

item.title: Light in the Darkness — Michael P. V. Barrett
item.description: Michael Barrett walks the whole book of Judges in 143 pages - the sin cycles, the flawed deliverers, and the faithful God behind them all. A short, redemptive-historical read from Ligonier that preaches Christ from one of the Bible's hardest books.

item.title: The Justification of the Sinless — Brendan Case
item.description: Would the Son have become incarnate had we never sinned? Case takes the old scholastic question seriously and builds a constructive Christology out of it.

item.title: Ready to Preach — Matthew D. Kim
item.description: This introductory homiletics textbook gives students and pastors a step-by-step process for crafting and communicating biblical sermons that are theologically grounded, culturally aware, and spiritually formed

item.title: Navigating Tough Texts of the Old Testament, Volume 1 — Tremper Longman III
item.description: As we read through the Bible, it's common to encounter puzzling or confusing passages. This is especially the case with the Old Testament, since its time and cultural setting are so far removed from our own. It's tempting to skip over these problem passages in our personal Bible study or in our preaching and teaching. But if all Scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting, and training in righteousness, those passages were preserved for our benefit.

item.title: With Me in the Valley — David Gibson
item.description: In this concise booklet, David Gibson examines the believer's union with Christ as the sheep and the shepherd depicted in Psalm 23, offering readers comfort in the hope of trusting him.

item.title: Persuasive Preaching — David R. Helm & Jeremy Meeks
item.description: This 9Marks book offers practical tips on public speaking that pastors can apply in their sermons to bring clarity, spark interest, and demonstrate care for their audiences.

item.title: God's Presence with Us and in Us: A Biblical Theology of the Holy Spirit — Miguel Echevarría · ESBT series
item.description: A whole-Bible study of the Spirit's presence, tracing the theme from Eden to the new creation.

item.title: Why We Worship: Experiencing Heaven on Earth at Church — Adriel Sanchez
item.description: A pastoral case for gathered worship as a foretaste of heaven.

item.title: Reformation and Tradition — Joshua Benjamins
item.description: Does the Reformation stand against the church’s ancient tradition, or grow out of it? These collected essays take up the legacy of Nicene theology and make the case that the Reformers were heirs of the early church’s creedal confession rather than its critics—a thoughtful entry in the renewed conversation over what Nicaea still means for Protestant faith.

item.title: A Path for Cultural Analysis — Vern Poythress
item.description: To understand our world, we don’t need more secular theories; we need more Scripture. In A Path for Cultural Analysis, Vern S. Poythress replaces broken modern frameworks with a distinctly biblical roadmap for the twenty-first century.
